incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV-2 alert: sudden spike in eviction errors and cross-tier routing. Traffic that should be staying in hosted is being routed into Dedicated pools for multiple tenants (~18 tenants observed). Auto-page sent to oncall. Logs: `eviction_count > 500min` and `route_policy: fallback-tier=dedicated`
Maya (SRE): I'm on it — pulling routing logs and recent policy deploys. Anyone who touched tier routing in last 2 hours?
Sam (Runtime): that was me, pushed a small change to the smart-routing policy to add region fallback. rolling back now if it looks related.
Priya (Platform): I see a config flip: `tier_preference: hosted, dedicated` -> `tier_preference: hosted -> dedicated` diff looks like an accidental priority bump for dedicated.
Maya (SRE): copy. Sam, can you revert and we can gate a quick patch?
Sam (Runtime): starting revert. command: ```git rev-parse --short HEAD && git revert --no-edit 4f2a1b7 && ./deploy routing-policy --env prod --tag hotfix-tier-revert```
Jorge (Support): getting customer reports in support queue — a handful of high-traffic tenants saw 502s + elevated latency when their requests hit dedicated pools that didn't have the expected model variants. Flagging top 3 customers: acme, zenhealth, learnly.
Anna (PM): prioritizing outreach. Jorge, can you confirm which customers had data plane errors vs degraded latency?
Jorge (Support): acme: 502 errors on text-generation endpoints. zenhealth: increased p99 from 220ms -> 2.1s. learnly: error spike then fallback to smaller model variant, degraded quality.
Maya (SRE): Evidence of wrong model variant assignment in logs when requests moved to dedicated. Example entry: ```[1719987602] tenant=acme route=dedicated-pool-42 model=redwood-large-v1 expected=redwood-large-v1-quantized?=false actual=redwood-large-v1-8bit``` That mismatch caused OOM/ejection.
Sam (Runtime): revert deployed. Observability shows routing policy reverted at `1719987720`. But traffic didn't fully stabilize — I'm seeing spillback loops where host-agent tries hosted->dedicated->hosted. Could be cached route decisions in edge routers.
Maya (SRE): ok next step: isolate dedicated pools serving affected tenants. We should cordon/drainthem so they'll fall back to hosted correctly. Priya, can platform cordon pool-42 and mark it draining?
Priya (Platform): doing cordon now. command: ```rbctl pool cordon pool-42 --reason "misrouted-tier-eviction" && rbctl pool drain pool-42 --timeout 300s```
incident-bot: pool cordon initiated by Priya at 1719987784.
Sam (Runtime): edges have cached route decisions for ~60s TTL; but I'm also flushing local edge caches with `edgectl flush --selector tier-routing`. Executed at 1719987796.
Maya (SRE): starting impact assessment. Querying token counts and OOMs per tenant. initial quick numbers: total evictions 1.2k in last 10m, 18 unique tenants, 4 tenants with >200 errors.
Jorge (Support): created temporary status updates for acme and zenhealth. acme flagged as partial outage. zenhealth marked as degraded. Links: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1719987654
Anna (PM): fine. I'll prepare messaging draft for enterprise customers. Want to be transparent about misroute and mitigation plan.
Maya (SRE): Mitigation summary so far: - reverted routing policy - cordoned offending dedicated pools - flushed edge caches - drained affected connections - enabled model variant strictness check (prevent auto-downconvert on pool mismatch)
Sam (Runtime): adding a temporary hard guard in the router: disallow tier switch for tenants with pinned isolation. Applying via feature-flag: `feature.tier_switch_hard_guard=true` -> applied at 1719987850.
Priya (Platform): drain shows 82 active connections; graceful drain in progress. ETA ~2m.
Maya (SRE): After drains and cache flush, error rates dropping but not zero. p95 latency for hosted now back to 300ms from 2.1s; acme 502s reduced by 90%.
Jorge (Support): customers are already replying to status posts. acme wants an RCA and timeline. I've scheduled a customer bridge at +30m.
Anna (PM): good. We'll coordinate on RCA postmortem and post-incident follow-ups. Assign owners: Sam for runtime root cause, Priya for pool lifecycle automation, Maya for incident timeline and mitigations, Jorge for customer comms.
Priya (Platform): postmortem action: add verification in pool claim path to ensure model-variant compatibility and tenant isolation metadata enforcement.
Sam (Runtime): preliminary root cause: a recent policy change unintentionally reordered fallback weights so dedicated became higher priority for certain region/routing combos. That plus a missing strict-variant check caused requests to land on incompatible dedicated nodes -> evictions.
Maya (SRE): Note for follow-up: introduce a canary gate for routing policy changes and add automated rollback on surge of evictions within 15m.
incident-bot: pager acknowledged by Maya (SRE) at 1719987658.
Maya (SRE): handing off for 2nd-tier analysis to Sam. I'll remain in the thread for customer comms. If anything spikes, ping me.
Sam (Runtime): taking over analysis. I'll run a targeted sim to reproduce policy reorder behavior and prepare a patch.
Jorge (Support): support notes: tracked affected tenants and ticket IDs in spreadsheet. Will attach logs and times for RCA.
Anna (PM): set a follow-up sync in 2 hours to review RCA outline and customer messaging.
Maya (SRE): final live update: metrics look stable. closing on-call bridge in 5m. Will convert this thread into a postmortem draft afterwards. Great teamwork everyone. :handshake:
Sam (Runtime): will open PR with policy validation and a test ensuring fallback weights cannot bump dedicated above hosted by mistake.
Priya (Platform): noted. Also adding a quick observability alert: 'routing-tier-change-anomaly' for future early detection.
incident-bot: incident status -> mitigation in place. next steps: RCA, customer comms, postmortem. Thread closed to oncall at 1719987960.
